The must-sees

  • Helsinki Cathedral

    Church · 1852

    Designed by Carl Ludvig Engel, it was finished in 1852, twelve years after his death. It was first named St. Nicholas’ Church after the Russian tsar Nicholas I.

    Look for: Inside, the plain white church holds statues of Martin Luther, Philipp Melanchthon and Mikael Agricola, who brought the Reformation to Finland.

  • Helsinki Central Station

    Station · 1919

    Designed by Eliel Saarinen, it was completed in 1919. The lantern holders by the entrance are among the best-known faces of Helsinki.

  • Market Square

    Market

    Stalls sell berries, fish and handicrafts much of the year. Boats to Suomenlinna leave from its quay.

    Look for: Find the granite obelisk with a double-headed eagle: the Empress’s Stone, from 1835, the oldest public monument in Helsinki.

  • Oodi Central Library

    Culture · 2018

    It opened in December 2018 as a project marking a century of Finnish independence. Visitors can borrow books, sew, 3D-print or simply sit on the top-floor terrace.

    Look for: On the top floor, the white ceiling ripples over one open hall of books, known as Book Heaven.

  • Senate Square

    Square

    Carl Ludvig Engel designed the square after Helsinki became the capital in 1812. The statue of Tsar Alexander II at its centre dates from 1894.

    Look for: Around the base of the tsar’s statue, four figures stand for Law, Peace, Light and Labour.

  • Sibelius Monument

    Landmark · 1967

    Eila Hiltunen’s monument to Jean Sibelius was unveiled in 1967. The face was added after debate over the abstract design.

    Look for: Step underneath the pipes and look up through them at the sky.

  • Suomenlinna

    Fortress

    Sweden began building it in 1748, when Finland was part of the Swedish realm, under Augustin Ehrensvärd. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and home to about 800 residents.

    Look for: In the main courtyard of the fortress, find the tomb of Augustin Ehrensvärd, buried in the stronghold he built.

  • Temppeliaukio Church

    Church · 1969

    Designed by the brothers Timo and Tuomo Suomalainen, it was completed in 1969. The bare rock walls give it acoustics that draw concerts as well as services.

    Look for: Look up: the dome is a coil of copper strip, resting on a ring of skylights cut between it and the rock.

  • Uspenski Cathedral

    Church · 1868

    Completed in 1868, it is often called the largest Orthodox church in Western Europe. Its bricks came from the Bomarsund fortress in Åland, destroyed in the Crimean War.

    Look for: Inside, look for the gilded iconostasis, the screen of icons before the altar.

How it works

  1. Open Wizzy in Helsinki and tap Start walk, or pick a ready-made walk.
  2. Put your phone in your pocket. Wizzy runs in the background, even with the screen locked.
  3. When you pass a place, you get a ping. Open it for the story, or keep walking.

Every place you see gets stamped in your Helsinki passport. Your location stays on your phone. No ads, no tracking.
